subject: Post-call summary: vector infra fit and cost/latency constraints
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@shopnexus.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@shopnexus.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: vector infra fit + next steps (ShopNexus)

Hi Alicia / Daniel —

Thanks for the time today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so we can validate fit quickly. Please correct anything I missed.

Quick recap (pain points):
- Search relevance has regressed as catalogue grows (currently ~220M product vectors).
- Rerank stage is the costly part: each page view triggers 8–12 candidate reranks, pushing per-request cost up.
- Current stack (prod): Milvus for vector index (cloud-managed), S3 for embedding store, application-layer reranker implemented in house on CPU nodes.
- Latency goal (existing): p95 end-to-end ≤ 180ms; target for new flow: p95 ≤ 120ms for the retrieval+rerank path.
- Unit cost pressure: want < $0.0008 per full-request (retrieve+rerank) at 100qps sustained.

Key success criteria you mentioned:
- Relevance at least parity with current reranker (A/B), with measurable mAP lift on the “top-10” testset.
- Predictable unit economics under holiday traffic (10–12x baseline).
- Ops surface: must expose per-model token/embedding cost breakdown and traceable latency by stage.

Technical notes we captured:
- Average vector dim: 1,024; average query top-k = 300 candidates retrieved; reranker scores top 50 for final sort.
- Typical batch patterns: most requests are single-turn interactive traffic; however index rebuilds and nightly bulk ingest run large batches (200k–1M vectors).
- KV cache is cold often due to query diversity; warm-cache hit rate currently ~12%.

Proposed next steps:
1) You to share a representative sample (anonymized) of 25k queries + candidate sets so we can run a relevance simulation (we mentioned a short NDA for data).
2) Redwood to run a 3-day micro-benchmark: retrieval latency matrix (p50/p95) across Milvus vs. Redwood-managed index, and cost simulation for 3 traffic profiles.
3) Technical deep-dive with Karthik + infra (30–45m) to validate batch IO patterns and caching strategy (we suggested Mon 10/26 or Tue 10/27).
4) Share our cost model + suggested quantization/replica setup (attachment: redwood-embed-cost-model-v1.xlsx).

Please confirm dates for the deep-dive and whether you can drop the 25k-sample by EOD Monday. If you prefer, we can accept a redacted CSV with: query_id, query_text, candidate_ids, current_score.

Thanks — feel free to add any missing constraints.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-embed-cost-model-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@shopnexus.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@shopnexus.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: vector infra fit + next steps (ShopNexus)

Thanks Vivek — this looks right and is super helpful. Couple quick clarifications: 

- The 220M number I quoted is our current online index (hot tier); we also have ~1.1B cold vectors in long-term store for historical queries.
- Our current top-k retrieval is 500 but we only re-rank 60 on average; we'll send a sample of 30k queries with candidates (anonymized) — Daniel will drop the CSV into the Drive link you shared.
- Holiday traffic: our projection is a 9x increase, but most of that is read-heavy (retrieval); reranker scale increases by ~4x.

On timelines: Monday 10/26 morning works for the deep-dive. We’ll aim to have the sample in the Drive by EOD Monday — if anything slips we’ll flag it.

One operational ask up front: can you include an analysis of cold-KV impacts? We’ve seen big p95 hops when cold caches are hit.

Thanks — Alicia
VP Product, ShopNexus
[ShopNexus — Platform]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@shopnexus.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: vector infra fit + next steps (ShopNexus)

Adding a few technical checkpoints we’ll cover in the deep-dive so we can size the correct instance/replica mix:

- Retrieval perf matrix: index type (IVF-Flat / HNSW / PQ), shard count, memory footprint per shard, and p50/p95 for 1k/5k/20k candidate scenarios.
- Reranker throughput: baseline CPU vs Redwood-optimized GPU path (batch sizes, kv-cache reuse). We need to know current average tokens per rerank call (roughly the text length + metadata) — if you can redaction-friendly sample that, it helps.
- Batch ingestion: peak ingest throughput and whether you can accept paused rebuilds during low-traffic windows. Our initial sizing assumes async bulk loads up to 500k vectors/hour.
- Cost targets: to hit < $0.0008/request at 100qps we’ll likely recommend a mix of quantized model backends + 2-tier indexing (hot HNSW + cold PQ snapshots).

Action items for the meeting (Karthik):
- I’ll bring a short runbook template for canarying model rollouts and fallback policies.
- Vivek will run the initial micro-benchmark and share results + kv-batch-patterns.csv.

If anyone has additional constraints (data residency, SOC2 evidence requests) drop them here and we’ll fold into the checklist.

-Karthik
Director, Solutions Architecture — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: kv-batch-patterns.csv (csv)]
